# Musi Full LLM Context

> Full inline briefing for LLMs working on the Musi language and repository. This complements `llms.txt`, which is the concise index. Prefer repository files as source of truth when this file conflicts with code, grammar, specs, or tests.

## Project Summary

Musi is an expression-first programming language with typed effects, a SEAM bytecode pipeline, package tooling around `.ms` source files, Rust compiler/runtime/tooling crates, and a first-party standard library. The workspace version is `0.1.0`; language contracts are frozen for the 0.1.0 baseline.

Two user-facing binaries ship from the workspace:

- `musi`: package/workspace lane for manifests, workspaces, run, build, and test flows.
- `music`: direct lane for single `.ms` source graphs and `.seam` artifacts.

Core namespace rules:

- `musi:*` is compiler-owned foundation and runtime capability space.
- `@std/<family>` is the first-party standard library surface.
- `@std` is a barrel module that re-exports stdlib families.
- `*.test.ms` files export `test`; `musi test` discovers tests recursively, including under `__tests__/`.

## Install And Quick Start

Prerequisites:

- Rust `1.95.0` or newer.
- `libffi` for native/FFI runtime support.

Local install:

```bash
cargo install --locked --force --path crates/music
cargo install --locked --force --path crates/musi
```

Package quick start:

```bash
musi init hello
cd hello
musi run
musi test
```

Direct file quick start:

```musi
let base := 21;

let twice (x : Int) : Int := x + x;

let total := twice(base);
total;
```

```bash
music check index.ms
```

## Command Surface

Package lane:

```bash
musi check
musi build
musi run
musi test
```

Direct lane:

```bash
music check index.ms
music build index.ms
music info index
music disasm index
music run index.seam
```

Validation commands commonly used in this repository:

```bash
make check
make lint
make rscheck
cargo test -p music_syntax
cargo test -p music_sema
```

Prefer targeted crate tests over full-workspace tests on lower-memory machines.

## Repository Layout

Top-level areas:

- `crates/`: Rust compiler, runtime, tooling, package, LSP, and CLI crates.
- `lib/std/`: first-party `@std` Musi package.
- `crates/musi_foundation/modules/`: compiler-owned `musi:*` foundation modules.
- `docs/reference/`: language/runtime/diagnostics/API references.
- `docs/where/`: ownership and workspace maps.
- `specs/`: language, runtime, interop, and SEAM design documents.
- `grammar/`: grammar sources and generated ANTLR artifacts.
- `benches/`: Criterion and VM/runtime benchmark support.

Canonical docs:

- `docs/where/workspace-map.md`
- `docs/reference/public-api.md`
- `docs/reference/language-feature-coverage.md`
- `docs/reference/builtins.md`
- `docs/reference/comments.md`
- `docs/reference/diagnostics.md`
- `docs/reference/performance.md`
- `docs/reference/seam-il.md`

Canonical grammar:

- `grammar/MusiParser.g4`
- `grammar/MusiLexer.g4`
- `grammar/Musi.abnf`

## Workspace Crate Map

Compiler pipeline:

- `music_base`: shared source spans, diagnostics, source maps.
- `music_builtin`: hidden builtin type, intrinsic, std/foundation registry.
- `music_names`: symbol interning and compiler name tables.
- `music_syntax`: lexer, parser, syntax tree.
- `music_module`: module keys, import maps, module syntax helpers.
- `music_resolve`: name and import resolution.
- `music_sema`: semantic checking, exported surface, effect rows.
- `music_ir`: IR model and diagnostics.
- `music_ir_lower`: sema-to-IR lowering.
- `music_emit`: SEAM emission from IR.
- `music_session`: end-to-end compile orchestration and caches.

Runtime and host:

- `music_seam`: SEAM artifact, SEAM HIL, lowered `.seam` text, binary, opcodes.
- `musi_vm`: VM program loading, values, execution, host/loader traits, VM errors.
- `musi_native_ffi`: libffi-backed native call bridge.
- `musi_native`: host effect and native dispatch.
- `musi_rt`: embeddable runtime wrapper around session, VM, and native host.
- `musi_foundation`: compiler-owned `musi:*` modules.

Project and tooling:

- `musi_project`: package manifests, workspace graph, registry, project compile entrypoints.
- `musi_fmt`: source formatting options, source formatter, path formatter.
- `musi_tooling`: diagnostics collection, hover, direct tooling helpers, editor primitives.
- `musi_lsp`: language server.

User-facing binaries:

- `music`: direct file and artifact lane.
- `musi`: package/workspace lane.

Supporting crates:

- `music_arena`: arena and slice-index utilities.
- `music_hir`: HIR data model.
- `music_term`: syntax and type term helpers.

Primary phase DAG:

- `music_base -> music_names -> music_syntax -> music_module -> music_resolve -> music_sema -> music_ir`
- `music_ir + music_sema -> music_ir_lower -> music_session`
- `music_ir -> music_emit -> music_session`
- `music_seam -> musi_vm -> musi_native -> musi_rt`
- `musi_foundation`, `musi_project`, and `musi_tooling` sit above core compiler/runtime crates.

## Public API Inventory

Binaries:

- `music`: direct check/build/run lane for `.ms` and `.seam`.
- `musi`: package-aware check/build/run/test lane.

Compiler libraries:

- `music_syntax`: lex/parse entrypoints and syntax tree exports.
- `music_builtin`: builtin type and intrinsic catalog used by compiler/runtime layers.
- `music_resolve`: resolved module model.
- `music_sema`: `check_module`, semantic surface, diagnostics, checked type metadata.
- `music_ir`: IR model and diagnostics.
- `music_ir_lower`: sema-to-IR lowering.
- `music_emit`: IR-to-SEAM lowering.
- `music_session`: `Session`, `CompiledOutput`, session diagnostics/options, CTFE host configuration.

Runtime libraries:

- `music_seam`: SEAM artifact encode/decode, SEAM HIL model/verifier, lowered `.seam` text, instruction/types surface.
- `musi_vm`: `Program`, `Vm`, `VmOptions`, `MvmMode`, `MvmFeatures`, `VmOptimizationLevel`, runtime `Value`, bound call handles, value inspection views, host/loader traits, VM errors.
- `musi_native`: `NativeHost`, native test report types.
- `musi_rt`: `Runtime`, `RuntimeOptions`, runtime errors.
- `musi_foundation`: compiler-owned foundation/runtime module registration helpers.

Project and tooling libraries:

- `musi_project`: project load, workspace/package compile entrypoints.
- `musi_fmt`: `FormatOptions`, source formatter, path formatter, formatter errors.
- `musi_tooling`: diagnostics collection, hover, artifact helpers.
- `musi_lsp`: `MusiLanguageServer`.

Internal/support libraries:

- `music_base`, `music_arena`, `music_hir`, `music_module`, `music_names`, `music_term`.

## Language Core

Musi is expression-first: everything is an expression. Top-level statements require `;`. In computation blocks, non-final expressions require `;`; a final expression may omit `;` and becomes the block result.

```musi
(
  let x := 1;
  x + 1
)
```

Delimiter meanings:

- `( ... )`: computation, grouping, blocks, tuple expressions, and sequencing.
- `{ ... }`: structure, records, data bodies, shapes, and attributes.
- `[ ... ]`: array/type-argument/index shape where grammar admits it.

Accepted empty forms:

```musi
()        -- unit
[,]       -- empty array
[;]       -- empty stack effect
data {;}  -- empty product
data {|}  -- empty sum
match x (|) -- empty match for uninhabited subject
```

Binding, assignment, and equality:

- `:=` binds a value or assigns into an existing mutable place.
- Assignment returns `()`.
- Equality is `=`.
- Inequality is `/=`.

Control:

- `if` is binary `Bit` selection and always has `else`.
- `match` is structural inspection. Alternatives start with `|`.
- Guards use `where`.
- `let pattern := expr else fallback;` is refutable forward binding.

```musi
if count /= 0 then use(count) else 0

match value (
| .Some(x) where x > 0 => x
| .Some(_) => 0
| .None => fallback
)
```

Functions and calls:

- Lambdas start with `\`.
- Function types use `->`.
- Declarations use `:` for result types.
- Named arguments use `name := value`.
- Pipelines use `|>`.

```musi
let id[T](value : T) : T := value;
let f := \(x : Int) : Int => x;
let result := value |> transform(extra := 1);
```

Fixed source operators:

```text
arithmetic: + - * / %
comparison: = /= < <= > >=
words: and or xor not in
ranges: ..< ..
fallback: ??
pipeline: |>
```

Users may not invent symbolic operators. `and`, `or`, `xor`, and `not` are strict value operators. Use `if`, `match`, or explicit delayed helpers for short-circuiting behavior.

## Types And Data

Primitive and library types:

- `Bit` is the primitive condition type. Conditions require `Bit`; there is no truthiness.
- `Bool` is a standard-library item, not a primitive keyword. It binds `.True` to bit value `1` and `.False` to bit value `0`, and exports lowercase aliases `true` and `false`.
- `Unknown` is an inference or recovery type.
- `Unit` has exactly one value and is written `()`.
- `Empty` is uninhabited.

Data definitions:

```musi
let Buffer := data {
  let ptr : Ptr[mut Byte];
  let len : Nat;
};

let Maybe[T] := data {
| Some(value : T)
| None
};
```

Do not mix product fields and sum variants in one `data` body.

Mutability:

```musi
let x := mut 0;
let x : mut Int := mut 0;
let p : Ptr[mut Byte] := getMutablePtr();
let q : mut Ptr[mut Byte] := mut getMutablePtr();
```

Absence and failure are algebraic data:

```musi
?T   == Maybe[T]
E!T  == Expect[T, E]
```

`??` is Maybe fallback only. Failure is handled with `match`, `let ... else`, or named helpers. There is no hidden exception syntax.

Ranges:

```musi
a ..< b   -- half-open [a, b)
a .. b    -- inclusive [a, b]
```

`...` remains spread/splat syntax and is lexed before range tokens.

## Imports, Exports, Modules, And External Boundaries

Top-level declarations are private by default. `export` adds a binding to the public Musi API.

```musi
export let add(a : Int, b : Int) : Int := (
  a + b
);
```

`export hidden let` exports a type name while hiding its representation.

```musi
export hidden let File := data {
  let fd : Word;
};
```

`import` brings in a Musi source export record. Bound imports are ordinary values.

```musi
let io := import "@std/io";
let std := import "@std";
let maybe := std.maybe;
```

`as` is not import alias syntax. It aliases matched or refined values only.

External boundaries use `@foreign` metadata on ordinary declarations. There is no `native`, `extern`, `pub`, or `foreign` source keyword in the small core.

Rules:

- `@foreign` plus a declaration without a body imports an external implementation.
- `@foreign` plus `export` plus a body exports an external entry point.
- `export` without `@foreign` is a public Musi API only.
- `@foreign` without `export` but with a body is invalid.
- `@foreign` with `export` but without a body is invalid in the core.
- Do not duplicate direction with `mode`, `import`, or `export` keys.

```musi
@foreign(
  name := "musi_read",
  abi := .c,
  stack := [Word, Ptr[Byte], Nat ; Nat]
)
let readFd(fd : Word, ptr : Ptr[Byte], len : Nat) : Nat;
```

## Attributes, Builtins, And Intrinsics

Accepted public source attributes:

```text
@deprecated
@skip
@layout
@foreign
@link
@target
```

Attribute names and keys use camelCase where needed.

`@link` carries native library link requirements for foreign bindings.

`@target` carries target/platform availability predicates.

Compiler-owned builtin bindings use reserved namespaced metadata:

```musi
@musi.builtin(name := "Type")
export let Type := Type;
```

Irreducible runtime leaves use reserved intrinsic metadata:

```musi
@musi.intrinsic(name := "ptr.load")
let ptrLoad(ptr : CPtr) : Int;
```

Source-facing APIs should wrap intrinsic-backed leaves in ordinary Musi code.

Compiler-owned facts:

- `music_builtin` owns compiler builtin names, foundation module specs, std package file paths, and intrinsic symbols.
- `musi:core`, focused `musi:*` host/VM primitive modules, and `@std/*` expose stable public APIs over the hidden builtin layer.
- `Pin[T]` is a compiler-owned scoped pin capability created only by `pin value as name in expr`.
- External boundary facts are modeled with `@foreign` metadata, stack effects, explicit unsafe surfaces, and ordinary import/export records.

## Shapes And Capability Values

`shape` defines a static interface or contract shape. Musi small core uses ordinary values and parameters for capability flow.

```musi
let Reader := shape {
  let read(into : mut Buffer) : IOError!Nat;
};
```

A concrete value can satisfy a shape statically. An `erased Shape` value may carry runtime evidence, witnesses, or dynamic dispatch. Type-erasure cost stays visible.

Capability values are ordinary values passed through normal bindings, imports, and parameters. They carry authority explicitly; there is no hidden global instance registry or ambient effect context.

```musi
let useReader(reader : erased Reader, buffer : mut Buffer) : IOError!Nat := (
  reader.read(buffer)
);
```

Operator members may appear in shapes, but operator precedence and associativity are fixed by the grammar, not user declarations.

## Comments And Documentation Comments

Ordinary comments:

```musi
-- line comment

/-
block comment
-/
```

Item docs attach to the following item:

```musi
--- value shown in examples
let value := 1;

/-- value shown in examples -/
let other := 2;
```

Module docs attach to the current module:

```musi
--! Math helpers used by examples.

/-!
Math helpers used by examples.
-/
```

Tooling extracts module docs for module hover and import documentation.

## Diagnostics Contract

Musi diagnostics follow Clang-style precision: exact source location, concrete subject, expected/found facts, related source ranges, and fix-its when safe.

Rules:

- Every user-facing diagnostic comes from typed diagnostic enums in the owning crate/phase.
- Every source diagnostic has one primary label on the offending token or expression.
- Headlines name the exact broken thing when known: source text, symbol, operator, field, variant, import specifier, type, `mut`, `known`, or expected/found pair.
- Secondary labels point to related source: declaration, expected annotation, parameter, previous definition, operation signature.
- Hints explain actionable repair.
- Fix-its only when replacement is exact and safe.
- Headlines avoid articles: `a`, `an`, `the`.
- Headlines avoid filler words: `was`, `were`, `is`.
- User-facing text does not abbreviate words like `arg`, `attr`, `expr`, or `fn`.

Renderer shape:

```text
src/main.ms:7:8: error[MS3091]: call argument `value` expected `String`, found `Int`
  |
7 | repeat(value := 10)
  |        ^^^^^ argument provided here
  |        ~~~~~ parameter `value` declared here with type `String`
help: pass string value or change parameter type
```

## Foundation Modules

Compiler-owned foundation/runtime modules live under `crates/musi_foundation/modules/`. They expose lower-level `musi:*` surfaces and back stdlib wrappers.

Important foundation module files:

- `core.ms`
- `crypto_host.ms`
- `encoding_host.ms`
- `env.ms`
- `fmt.ms`
- `fs.ms`
- `io.ms`
- `json_host.ms`
- `log.ms`
- `process.ms`
- `random.ms`
- `syntax.ms`
- `test.ms`
- `text.ms`
- `time.ms`
- `uuid_host.ms`

Use `@std/*` first in user code. Use `musi:*` when working at compiler, runtime, host integration, or intrinsic boundaries.

SEAM is the artifact and bytecode pipeline target.

Key references:

- `docs/reference/seam-il.md`
- `specs/seam/domains.md`
- `specs/seam/format.md`
- `specs/seam/bytecode.md`

Runtime and interop references:

- `specs/runtime/memory-model.md`
- `specs/runtime/interop.md`
- `specs/interop/c-interop-memory.md`

Runtime implementation crates:

- `music_seam`: artifact encode/decode, HIL, text, binary, instructions.
- `musi_vm`: VM program loading, values, execution, host and loader traits.
- `musi_native_ffi`: libffi-backed native call bridge.
- `musi_native`: host effect and native dispatch.
- `musi_rt`: embeddable runtime wrapper.

## Formatter, Tooling, And LSP

Formatter:

- `musi_fmt` owns source formatting, path formatting, and `FormatOptions`.
- Formatter tests live in `crates/musi_fmt/src/tests.rs`.
- CLI and LSP formatting surfaces call into `musi_fmt`.

Tooling:

- `musi_tooling` owns diagnostics collection, hover, document links, folding ranges, selection ranges, references, rename, symbols, semantic tokens, code actions, and artifact helpers.
- Tooling APIs are CLI/editor-oriented and should return stable data structures over raw compiler internals.

LSP:

- `musi_lsp` owns `MusiLanguageServer`.
- LSP conversion helpers live under `crates/musi_lsp/src/server/convert.rs`.
- Request handlers live under `crates/musi_lsp/src/server/requests.rs`.
- Navigation helpers live under `crates/musi_lsp/src/server/navigation.rs`.

## Coding And Repo Rules

Important repository conventions:

- No placeholders in `crates/`: no `todo!()`, `unimplemented!()`, placeholder panics, or empty pipelines.
- `src/` is production-only.
- Rust unit tests live in `module/tests.rs`.
- Benches live in `benches/` and use Criterion with `bench_` prefix.
- Prefer longform names: `lexer.rs`, `parser.rs`, `syntax`, `sema`.
- Reserve `Syntax*` for syntax trees, not token streams.
- Lexer nouns stay short: `Token`, `TokenKind`, `Trivia`, `Lexer`.
- Keep trivia types in `trivia.rs`.
- Prefer top-level `use` imports and local names.
- Do not write fully qualified paths such as `music_hir::Foo`, `music_arena::Bar`, or `crate::mod::Type` inside function bodies, match arms, or helper signatures just to name ordinary types or variants.
- Absolute singleton uses are acceptable for real singletons such as `crate::CONST`, `crate::func()`, and macros.
- Do not introduce new macros.

Type alias rules:

- `Vec<Item>` becomes `ItemList`.
- `Box<Item>` becomes `ItemPtr` or `BoxedItem`.
- `Result<T, XError>` becomes `XResult<T = ()>`.
- If one composite type appears two or more times in one module public surface, alias it.
- Alias names describe the owned concept, not only the container shape.

Phase boundaries:

- Phase DAG has no cycles.
- SEAM transport stays `music_bc -> music_assembly`.
- Project integration lives above compiler/runtime phases in `musi_project` and `music_session`.
- Pre-resolve contracts use `*Env` names, not `*Resolver`.

## Lint And Validation Configuration

The workspace uses Rust 2024 and strict linting. Workspace lints deny unsafe code by default, many Clippy categories, placeholder APIs, unreachable code, TODOs, unimplemented code, and accidental absolute paths.

Common validation:

```bash
cargo fmt --all
cargo fmt --check
cargo check --workspace
cargo check --workspace --tests
cargo clippy --locked --workspace -- -D warnings
cargo clippy --locked --workspace --tests -- -D warnings
cargo test -p musi_diaggen -p music -p musi_fmt -p musi_tooling -p musi_lsp --tests
cargo run -p musi_diaggen -- check
make rscheck
make lint
```

`make rscheck` finds architecture, portability, naming, aliasing, and shape issues beyond standard Rust/Clippy signals.

## Agent Guidance

When answering questions or changing code:

- Treat grammar files and authored source as source of truth.
- Prefer current repository evidence over older docs if conflicts exist.
- Distinguish current implemented behavior from proposed design.
- For syntax questions, check grammar first, then specs/tests.
- For crate ownership questions, check `docs/where/workspace-map.md`.
- For public API questions, check `docs/reference/public-api.md`.
- For diagnostic wording or ranges, check `docs/reference/diagnostics.md` and typed diagnostic enums in the owning crate.
- For standard-library behavior, check `lib/std/`, `crates/musi_foundation/modules/`, and std tests.
- For runtime behavior, check `musi_rt`, `musi_native`, `musi_vm`, `music_seam`, and runtime specs.
- Avoid broad compatibility fallbacks, ad hoc diagnostics, parser fallbacks, or doc-only changes when code behavior is requested.
- Prefer focused edits and targeted validation.
